Answer: A
Reason: The coronal CT image shows a distinct, round, well-defined opacity in the right middle lobe region, which corresponds to the classic radiographic appearance of a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm (often surrounded by consolidation or hemorrhage given the history of haemoptysis). Options B through F describe findings (linear opacity, effusions, interstitial markings, cardiomegaly, granulomas) that are not the primary focal lesion visible in the right lung on this scan.
